author: TJ Jordan and Cécile Marchand
title: How a French Oil Executive Is Working With the Trump Administration to ‘Kill’ Europe’s Methane Plan
content:
A TotalEnergies executive is working with U.S. officials to delay the implementation of new European Union methane rules, raising questions over the company’s pledges to tackle leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.




François-Régis Mouton, formerly vice-president of gas advocacy at TotalEnergies, has been representing the International Association of Oil and Gas Producers (IOGP), a London-based fossil fuel lobby group, on an assignment from the French oil giant since 2018.




Mouton has repeatedly shared and engaged with hard right, anti-renewable energy and climate science-denial content on his personal social media, a review by DeSmog and French environmental newsroom Vert found.




Mouton, who serves as IOGP’s Europe managing director, met with U.S. federal officials on at least three occasions to discuss the European Union Methane Regulation (EUMR) in the past 14 months, according to social media posts. The new framework would force oil and gas importers to meet certain standards for methane leaks in their supply chains or face big fines.




In October 2025, Mouton visited the White House to brief the National Energy Dominance Council, a pro-fossil fuel Trump administration advisory body, on how the IOGP could “work together to address and remove regulatory barriers such as…the #EUMethaneRegulation,” according to LinkedIn

title: In Their Own Words: The Senior Reform and Tory Figures Who Have Lauded Trump
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump suffered a spectacular setback in the country’s midterm elections this week, with Democrats taking control of Congress and the Republicans losing races in their traditional heartlands.




The election was a rebuke to Trump’s increasingly 

unpopular presidency

. Voters expressed frustration with the cost of living and the economy, while the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran – which has driven up fuel prices – has proven to be a major political liability.




Trump’s political fortunes have also been damaged by his administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the agency at the centre of his mass deportation drive, has become a flashpoint and an emblem of Trump’s autocratic rule.




Yet, across the Atlantic, some of the UK’s most senior right-wing politicians have spent recent years enthusiastically praising Trump, celebrating his political leadership, and seeking to emulate his policies.




Reform UK

 leader 

Nigel Farage

declared

author: Mary Stuart
title: AI Needed to Produce More Gas to Power More AI, Tech Firm Cohere Says
content:
Oil and gas companies need to integrate AI into their operations so that they can extract more fossil fuels—which can then be used to power more AI.




That is the pitch that Canada’s leading AI company, Cohere, is making to the oil and gas industry, even as its CEO Aidan Gomez argues publicly that it is important for the tech industry to be aligned with “environmental goals.”




“As energy demand surges globally, driven in part by the explosive growth of AI data centers, oil and gas companies face significantly new operational, market, and environmental pressures,” explains a 

Cohere e-book

 from 2025 that advertises the AI company’s services to the fossil fuel sector. “AI has the potential to change the industry’s trajectory quickly, thereby better equipping it to address the growing supply-demand imbalance.”




An 

X post

 from the Toronto-based Cohere in early 2025 claimed that “AI-driven analytics optimize drilling, leading to more efficient resource extraction,” while predicting that “the oil and gas market for AI & ML [machine learning] is projected to surpass $4.9 billion by 2034, with GenAI playing a pivotal role in this growth.”




Using 

AI to increase the production of fossil fuels

, which are then used to power the explosive growth of AI data centres, might seem like a strategy designed mostly to increase profits for fossil fuel and tech companies.

title: Millions of Dollars Pouring into UK Democracy from Trump’s America
content:
MPs and leading UK think tanks have received major sums from U.S. benefactors – often with ties to U.S. President Donald Trump – since the 2024 general election, DeSmog can reveal. 




Six MPs, including 

Reform UK

Nigel Farage

Meanwhile, seven conservative policy groups in the UK have received at least $3 million (£2.3 million) from U.S. sources since 2024, and $20.4 million (£15.2 million) since 2016, the year of Trump’s first presidential election.




These revelations come as Trump’s Republican Party faces an uphill battle in today’s Midterm elections, with the Democrats vying to win control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Trump’s poll numbers have 

hit new lows

Trump is also 

unpopular

author: Edward Donnelly and Rei Takver
title: Revealed: Pro-AI Data Center Group Spending At Least $2.54M on TV Ads to Influence Ohio Election
content:
A pro-AI data center group purchased at least $2.54 million worth of television ads that ran recently in Ohio, a new DeSmog analysis reveals. The group, Build American AI, is linked to Leading the Future, a major AI industry super PAC backed by Silicon Valley billionaires.




The ads extolled the economic benefits of Ohio’s data center boom, one of the hottest issues in the state’s Senate election, but did not endorse either candidate in the race: Trump-aligned Republican incumbent Jon Husted, who was appointed by Governor Mike DeWine to serve out Vice President J.D. Vance’s term, and former three-term Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown.




“When some people hear data centers they picture computers and servers,” says one Build American AI ad. “But we see something different: electricians, engineers, manufacturers.” The ad states that data centers have brought more than $40 billion in investments and created over 95,000 jobs in Ohio.




“The future won’t be built by politicians or special interests,” 

states

 the ad, “It’ll be built by American workers right here in Ohio.”




The ads appeared on at least 16 Ohio television stations between September 7 and October 21, according to Build American AI’s 

filings

 with the Federal Communications Commission, which described them as “non-candidate issue ads.”

author: Justin Nobel
title: Ohio Denies Evidence of Fracking Waste in Drinking Water. Its Own Records Show Otherwise.
content:
This story was co-published with Rolling Stone.




In Ohio’s rural southeastern corner, Marietta College geology professor David Jeffrey was among the residents worried that industry activity in America’s booming natural gas region could be polluting their drinking water. That’s “the biggest fear,” he said at an August meeting with top Ohio officials.




When Jeffrey and residents from advocacy groups Buckeye Environmental Network and Washington County for Safe Drinking Water met with Ohio officials, those state officials repeatedly assured residents that despite the up to 1.4 billion gallons of oil and gas wastewater injected in underground wells in their county and across Ohio each year, the state was unaware of any resulting drinking water contamination there.




“We would have heard about it,” Mary Mertz, director of the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR), which oversees both aspects of Ohio’s environment and its oil and gas industry, told residents in the August 17 virtual meeting.




“No one has called us that I’m aware of,” said Eric Vendel, ODNR’s oil and gas division chief. “We have a water investigation form that can be filled out and we would have my team down there and investigate the water.”

author: Rachel Santarsiero
title: President Trump Unveils EPA’s New Contradictory Methane Proposal at Campaign Rally
content:
At a Tuesday campaign rally for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Lubbock, Texas, President Trump announced the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposal to roll back a Biden-era methane rule, setting up a likely future showdown in how the agency oversees climate pollution under the Clean Air Act.




The proposal marks a break from the agency’s previous approaches to greenhouse gas regulation by maintaining that — for now — the EPA still has the authority to regulate climate pollution from the oil and gas industry, though it might revisit this decision later. With affordability top of mind for many midterm voters, however, the President framed the move in economic terms.   




“Tonight I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations,” Trump announced to the crowd, located near the oil-rich Permian Basin. The new plan would loosen federal requirements for oil and gas operators to detect and repair leaks, ease restrictions on gas flaring, and eliminate the Super Emitter Program, a third-party monitoring and reporting system designed to identify major releases of methane, known as a 

climate super pollutant

.

content:

GB News

Sir Paul Marshall

All Perspectives Ltd

Marshall is also one of its two principal funders, pumping money into the

The Labour government last week approved the development of the Jackdaw gas field near Aberdeen and is expected to make a decision on Rosebank soon.

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s 

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.




Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.




The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.




DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.

author: Ellen Ormesher
title: Interactive Archive Shares Secrets of Shell’s Early Climate Research
content:
Campaigners backing attempts to sue Shell over a typhoon in the Philippines have launched an online archive showing that the British oil major knew that burning fossil fuels could harm the climate as early as the 1960s.

ExposeShell.com features documents including a 1966 memo Shell commissioned from British scientist James Lovelock and the ‘Greenhouse Effect’, a confidential 1988 report predicting that human-caused warming could trigger “dramatic” changes in sea level, ocean currents, weather and precipitation — “larger than any that have occurred over the last 12,000 years.” [Read these and other documents in the DeSmog series #ShellKnew]

The interactive site went live as Shell announced the latest figures showing that oil majors are enjoying bumper profits as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran pushes oil prices higher. Shell said its adjusted third-quarter earnings had doubled to £10.8 billion in comparison to the same period last year.

“We don’t need any more reports to us that this big oily industry has been creating disaster,” Robin Wells, director of Fossil Free London, one of the groups behind the website, said in a statement. “Shell researched the reality but tore up the truth and locked it in the dark. Now, we are all facing the disastrous consequences.”

title: Carney Almost as Bad as Trump on Climate, Emissions Watchdog Warns
content:
Canada’s already battered reputation on curbing climate emissions has become drastically worse under the leadership of Prime Minister Mark Carney according to a recent report card from 

Climate Action Tracker

, approaching levels of inaction comparable to the “drill baby drill” Trump Administration.




“Prime Minister Mark Carney has so far been unwilling to recommit to either the 2030 or 2035 targets and has conceded that, under his energy plan, Canada’s emissions will be higher in the near term than previously projected,” warned the report. “If Canada were to officially abandon its 2030 and 2035 targets, it would be the first country after the United States to do so.”




The emissions watchdog didn’t mince words about the pace and scale of Canada’s climate rollbacks.




“What is shocking to us is the true extent to which Prime Minister Carney has rolled back climate policies, largely in favour of the fossil fuel industry,” Bill Hare, CEO of Climate Analytics, a CAT partner, 

said in a release

.




“This Carney climate carnage, while not quite as bad as Trump’s, is rapidly heading in the same direction, despite the country being hit by record wildfires and other devastating climate impacts,” he added.

content:

during a speech earlier this month

Chamberlain is vice president for external affairs at the 

Edmund Burke Foundation

He is also senior counsel with the Article III Project, a MAGA group set up to fight against “lawfare,” which 

it describes as

author: Taylor Noakes
title: ‘Snipped And Posted’: How Pro-Oil Groups Generate Viral Content Online
content:
In December 2025, former B.C. Premier Christy Clark gave an interview on Global News where she described Canada’s west coast ban on oil tankers as a “ridiculous” constraint on the Canadian economy.




A clip of Clark’s interview then began to circulate online, where it was shared by several Canadian conservative influencers and aggregator accounts on platforms including X and Facebook with captions including “reality check,” “huge truth bomb” and “economic self-sabotage.”




Within days, the interview clip was spreading across the social media feeds of people in B.C. and beyond, eventually surpassing 1.6 million views.




But this was not necessarily a case of west coast residents suddenly deciding organically they wanted to overturn the ban on coastal oil tanker traffic brought in by former Liberal Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.




The digital media amplification of Clark’s comments was orchestrated in part by Canada Action, a pro-oil industry advocacy organization partly funded by 

Cenovus Energy

, Canada’s third-largest oil and gas company.




It was one example of “showcasing Canada Action’s content leadership influencing the public discussion,” according to an internal slidedeck from the Calgary-based group. That slidedeck, which hasn’t yet been reported on, was obtained by Greenpeace Canada and published in its October 2026 report 

Manufacturing Petro-Populism

.

author: Selene Magnolia Gatti, Santi Donaire and Clare Carlile
title: In Pictures: ‘Armageddon’ at Europe’s Swim Spots Linked to Climate Change and Factory Farm Pollution
content:
Across Brittany, tractors can be seen trundling onto beaches to remove truckloads of foul-smelling algae ahead of the tourist rush. 




Situated below steep cliffs and ancient forests, these once pristine beaches have been devastated by algal blooms – the rapid growth of toxic seaweed which kills off fish and plant life. This sea lettuce algae can also release a toxic gas that can cause humans dizziness, chest pain, breathing problems, and even cardiac arrest.




The French peninsula is not alone. Fed by harmful pollution from agriculture, and fuelled by seas warmed by climate change, lurid green blooms are increasingly appearing on beaches and lakes across Europe – prompting hundreds of swimming bans across the continent this summer. 






















 













 
















This article was published in partnership with 

Euronews

 and 

Climatica













Scientists are clear on the cause: for decades, chemicals including nitrogen and phosphorus have leached into waterways from human sewage, as well as fertilisers and excess manure fuelled by the rapid growth of Europe’s factory farms. 




These ‘nutrients’ are vital for plant growth – but in large quantities they destroy the delicate balance of ecosystems, allowing certain plants, including algae, to multiply at the expense of animals and other species.

author: Rachel Sherrington and Hazel Healy
title: How Big Pharma Tried to Weaken the Rules of the UN’s Nature Fund
content:
As the COP17 nature summit gets underway in Armenia, evidence has emerged of lobbying by a leading international pharmaceuticals group to weaken the terms of a flagship fund for nature.




Documents analysed by DeSmog show that the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations (IFPMA) 

called

 for a “radical rethink” of the rationale for the 

landmark

 Cali Fund – the first mechanism built to take voluntary payments from large companies that profit from genetic sequence data.




The IFPMA states that the “modalities of the decision” to establish the Fund – which was ratified by 196 countries in 2024 at the COP16 summit of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity in Colombia – should be “significantly reviewed, revised and clarified”.




In the consultation submission, the trade group – which 

represents

 the pharmaceutical sector at the UN – also challenged the indicative rates at which companies were invited to contribute to the Fund, agreed at COP16 as 0.1 percent of revenue or 1 percent of profit.

The IFPMA labelled these indicative rates as “premature”, set “without any rational analysis”, and “commercially unrealistic”, suggesting instead that companies be allowed to contribute to the voluntary fund at a level of their choosing.

author: Sam Bright
title: Reform Figure Behind ‘Shocking’ Grenfell Comments Still Involved in Party
content:
A former housing executive fired by 

Reform UK

 for making “shameful” comments about the 2017 Grenfell Tower tragedy still claims to have a role in the party, DeSmog can reveal.




Simon Dudley, a former chair of Homes England, was removed as the party’s housing spokesperson for making – 

in the words

 of Reform leader 

Nigel Farage

 – “shocking” and “deeply inappropriate” comments about the disaster.




In an interview with Inside Housing in April, Dudley said the deadly blaze, which led to the deaths of 72 people, was a “tragedy” but that “everyone dies in the end”. He claimed that rules introduced in the wake of the fire to improve safety standards were examples of “regulation which is not working”.




Dudley was roundly criticised for his remarks, including by groups representing Grenfell survivors and next of kin. The then prime minister Keir Starmer called the comments “shameful”.




However, despite being sacked as Reform’s housing spokesperson, Dudley still appears to work with the party.




He 

introduced

 Reform’s deputy leader and housing chief 

Richard Tice

 to business delegates at the party’s annual conference in September, and chaired a question and answer session following Tice’s speech.
